members.reason: [llm] duplicates #1961: Both PRs fix the same SSE reader-lock memory leak in src/client/streamableHttp.ts: the ReadableStream reader obtained via .getReader() in the SSE read loop is never released, pinning the underlying stream buffer (~50MB per long-lived client) in memory. Both wrap the identical `while (true) { const { value, done } = await reader.read(); ... }` block (same hunk starting at line 328) in a try block so the lock can be released when the loop exits.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs settle the pending JSON-mode response promise inside close(), but #2600's diff additionally clears _requestToStreamMapping (a correlation map #2692's diff does not touch), which its changeset documents as needed to stop a send() suspended in eventStore.storeEvent() from resuming against a retired correlation and leaking a response that can never be delivered. #2600 also states its close() fix is shared with NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport, which wraps this transport. #2692 settles the pending POST with a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error and explicitly groups outstanding request ids by stream for batched POSTs (reusing an already-set real response instead of overwriting it) — reviewers should confirm #2600's implementation preserves this batched-POST handling before closing #2692, since that edge case isn't mentioned in #2600's changeset.

members.title: fix(server): retire in-flight request state when the streamable HTTP transport closes
members.author: rxits
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves JSON-response-mode POST requests hanging forever: handleRequest()'s returned Promise<Response> is only resolved by send(), and close() tears down _streamMapping/_requestResponseMap without settling that pending promise, so the HTTP request stays open until the platform's own timeout fires. (2 PRs)
